feature.p: The "interactive" element embeds interactive material: GeoGebra, Desmos, CircuitJS, JSXGraph, general JavaScript, or an iframe. It has been rendering in HTML output for years and is widely used, but its large vocabulary of per-platform attributes, and the mechanism for static representations in print and PDF, are still evolving; expect attribute names, defaults, and required companions to shift before it enters the production schema.

An "eval" element substitutes the value of a named object from a dynamic (randomized) exercise into text or mathematics. It is part of the dynamic exercise vocabulary, under active development in concert with the Runestone platform, and both its name and its reach are still settling.

feature.elements: setup variable formula condition evaluation evaluate test de-object de-random de-number de-expression de-evaluate jsimports jslibrary config-json setupScript postRenderScript
feature.p: This element is part of the machinery for dynamic (randomized) exercises: a "setup" defines randomized objects, and an "evaluation" says how a reader's answers are checked. The whole vocabulary is under active development in concert with the Runestone platform and is among the most likely parts of PreTeXt to change.

Multiple-choice and True/False exercises structure their answers with "choices", "choice", and per-choice "feedback". This interactive exercise vocabulary is aligned with the Runestone platform; the markup is reasonably stable in practice, but the details (attributes, feedback placement) remain subject to change.

Parsons problems (re-ordering blocks of code or prose) structure their content with "blocks" and "block". This interactive exercise vocabulary is aligned with the Runestone platform and its markup, particularly around program languages and indentation, is still subject to change.

feature.elements: matching matches match premise response cardsort
feature.p: Matching and card-sorting exercises pair premises with responses. This interactive exercise vocabulary is aligned with the Runestone platform, and the markup for expressing the pairs is still subject to change.

feature.elements: areas area select itself for logic numcmp strcmp mathcmp jscmp
feature.p: This element supports the evaluation of fill-in-the-blank exercises: "areas"/"area" mark the blanks and the comparison elements say how a response is judged. The vocabulary is under active development in concert with the Runestone platform.

The "fillin" element itself is standard, but attributes supporting interactive fill-in exercises (such as a mode, a name binding the blank to an evaluation, or a width) are part of the dynamic exercise vocabulary still under development.

Within WeBWorK problems a "var" is standard. Elsewhere it marks a fill-in blank bound to the evaluation machinery of a dynamic exercise, and that use is part of the dynamic exercise vocabulary still under development.

Coding exercises place a "program" (typically rendered as an interactive ActiveCode) inside an exercise, possibly with attached data ("datafile") or unit tests; a "query" is an in-page poll or survey. These are aligned with the Runestone platform and their markup is still subject to change.

Several attributes here are experimental switches for interactive exercises (for example a programming language, or adaptive behavior). The attribute names and their values are aligned with the Runestone platform and may change.

A "static" or "dynamic" element supplies an alternate representation of an interactive exercise, for outputs (print, PDF, EPUB) that cannot run it. How representations are expressed and generated is still being worked out.

Attributes giving finer control over which solutions appear (selecting treatment of worksheet and reading questions, or limiting scope) are experimental; the attribute names and their value vocabularies may change.
A "myopenmath" element embeds a problem hosted by the MyOpenMath service. Support is functional but narrow, and the markup may change as the integration matures.
A "stack" element carries a STACK question (server-graded mathematics, backed by a Moodle/STACK server). The embedding markup is developing along with the server integration.

Richer front matter is under development: a "shortlicense" may carry footnotes, and a "website" may be structured with a name and an address. The final shape of structured bibliographic front matter is still being designed.
This element is an alternate flavor of "proof", intended to signal a different level of rigor. The eventual list of proof-like elements, and their names, are still under discussion.
